ai.description: This 40–50 mm frog has a yellowish-brown dorsum with a dark, hourglass-shaped marking. It features distinct white spots on the flanks and translucent, webbed feet. Family: Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates pseudocruciger* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, hourglass-shaped marking on its back, which is absent in similar *Polypedates* species.
ai.habitat: *Polypedates pseudocruciger* inhabits moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The False Hour-glass Tree Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation surrounding forest pools and streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates pseudocruciger* breeds during the monsoon, laying foam nests containing 100–200 eggs on vegetation overhanging water, into which tadpoles drop upon hatching.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates pseudocruciger* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Polypedates pseudocruciger* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed chirps typically heard near forest streams or stagnant pools.
